content: Amoxicillin capsules, chewable tablets, and oral suspensions can be administered without regard to meals. However, the 400 mg suspension, 400 mg chewable tablet, and 875 mg tablet have only been studied when taken at the start of a light meal. Food effect studies have not been conducted for the 200 mg and 500 mg formulations. Chewable tablets must be thoroughly chewed before swallowing. For neonates and infants aged 12 weeks or younger (≤3 months), the maximum recommended dose of amoxicillin is 30 mg/kg/day, divided and administered every 12 hours (q12h), due to their immature renal function, which affects drug elimination. For adults and pediatric patients older than 3 months, dosing for infections caused by less susceptible organisms should follow recommendations for severe infections. Pediatric dosing is intended for individuals weighing less than 40 kg. Children weighing 40 kg or more should follow adult dosing recommendations. Each strength of the suspension is also available as a chewable tablet for older children. After reconstitution, the required amount of suspension should be placed directly on the child’s tongue for swallowing or mixed with formula, milk, fruit juice, water, ginger ale, or cold drinks. These preparations should be consumed immediately and in their entirety to ensure the full dosage is received. Patients with gonorrhea should be evaluated for syphilis, as per laboratory testing precautions. Larger doses may be necessary for persistent or severe infections. In the treatment of chronic urinary tract infections, frequent bacteriological and clinical evaluations are essential. Smaller doses than those recommended should not be used, and higher doses may sometimes be required. For stubborn infections, therapy may need to continue for several weeks, with clinical and/or bacteriological follow-up for several months after treatment cessation. Except for gonorrhea, treatment should continue for at least 48 to 72 hours beyond the point when the patient becomes asymptomatic or evidence of bacterial eradication is obtained. For infections caused by Streptococcus pyogenes, a minimum of 10 days of treatment is recommended to prevent acute rheumatic fever. For Helicobacter pylori eradication to reduce the risk of duodenal ulcer recurrence, the following regimens are recommended: 1. Triple Therapy: Amoxicillin 1 gram, clarithromycin 500 mg, and lansoprazole 30 mg, all administered twice daily (q12h) for 14 days. 2. Dual Therapy: Amoxicillin 1 gram and lansoprazole 30 mg, each administered three times daily (q8h) for 14 days. Refer to the full prescribing information for clarithromycin and lansoprazole for contraindications, warnings, and dosing adjustments in elderly or renally impaired patients. For adults with impaired renal function, dose reduction is generally unnecessary unless renal impairment is severe. Patients with a glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of less than 30 mL/min should not receive the 875 mg tablet. For those with a GFR of 10 to 30 mL/min, 500 mg or 250 mg should be administered every 12 hours, depending on infection severity. For patients with a GFR of less than 10 mL/min, 500 mg or 250 mg should be administered every 24 hours, depending on infection severity. Hemodialysis patients should receive 500 mg or 250 mg every 24 hours, with an additional dose during and after dialysis. There are no specific dosing recommendations for pediatric patients with impaired renal function. Directions for Mixing Oral Suspension: Prepare the suspension at the time of dispensing. Tap the bottle to loosen the powder. Add approximately one-third of the total amount of water required for reconstitution, then shake vigorously to wet the powder. Add the remaining water and shake vigorously again. For the 200 mg/5 mL formulation, each teaspoonful (5 mL) will contain 400 mg of amoxicillin.
